key_findings: Chemogenetic activation of adult dorsal horn NPY-expressing inhibitory interneurons reduced acute pain, pruritogen-evoked itch, and inflammatory and neuropathic hypersensitivity, independent of Y1 receptor signalling and mediated predominantly by GABA.
Silencing NPY-INs exaggerated chloroquine itch and caused spontaneous itch/skin lesions in a GRPR-IN-dependent manner without changing nociceptive thresholds.
